title: Scheme-test restriction of quasi-coherent modules on a fibred fppf site
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with its big fppf site and structure sheaf as in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module, where quasi-coherent means locally admitting a presentation by direct sums of copies of the structure sheaf. For every object $x\in\mathcal C(T)$ there is a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-module $F_x$ [pqf-def-coherent], naturally determined up to unique compatible isomorphism, such that the restriction of $F$ to the slice over $x$ is the sheaf $(u:T'\to T)\mapsto\Gamma(T',u^*F_x)$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$; here $u^*$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. In particular $F(x)=\Gamma(T,F_x)$. For every arrow $y\to x$ over $u:T'\to T$ the canonical map $u^*F_x\to F_y$ is an isomorphism; these maps are natural in $F$ and satisfy the identity and composition compatibilities of tensor pullback. The scheme-test comparison is fully faithful on each slice and identifies the structure sheaf and tensor products with the ordinary structure sheaf and tensor products. If $F\to G$ is a morphism of quasi-coherent modules which is locally surjective as a map of sheaves on $\mathcal C_{fppf}$, the induced map $F_x\to G_x$ is surjective for every $x$. Conversely, if all $F_x\to G_x$ are surjective, then $F\to G$ is locally surjective. For any functor $a:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ of categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, precomposition $a^*F(d)=F(a(d))$ is quasi-coherent and is the tensor pullback on their big ringed fppf sites. These assertions impose no algebraicity, quasi-compactness, finiteness, or flatness hypothesis on $\mathcal C$, $a$, or the scheme tests.

source.place: Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), and Tag 06WH (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent); scheme comparison is descent.tex Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), part (1), with Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), parts (1), (3), (4), (7). Surjections here are sheaf surjections, not left exactness on the big site.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal C(T)$. The projection $\mathcal C/x\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ sends $z\to x$ to its base map. It is essentially surjective by existence of lifts in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; for two such objects, the unique-factorisation axiom gives exactly one arrow over every compatible base arrow. Thus it is fully faithful. Coverings on both sides are exactly the families whose base maps form fppf covers, and the structure rings agree objectwise. This proves the equivalence of ringed sites, without replacing $\mathcal C$ by isomorphism classes. The slice $\mathcal C/x$ is also fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ (pull a domain back and compose with its arrow to $x$). Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image] to its projection to $\mathcal C$. Restriction is a module-sheaf functor preserving free sums and cokernels. In the explicit local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], a presentation cover of any $z\to x$ is just a presentation cover of $z$ with its arrows composed to $x$. Its presentation is unchanged on the further slice, by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Consequently the restriction $R_xF$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 06W0 (lemma-localizing) and Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent), necessary direction; the proof uses only the explicit lifting axioms and local-presentation definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] with $V=T$ to $R_xF$. Its inverse gives the quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_x$ and a canonical counit $A_T(F_x)\simeq R_xF$, identity on the Zariski opens. Hence at $u:T'\to T$ its value is $\Gamma(T',u^*F_x)$, and at the terminal object it gives $F(x)=\Gamma(T,F_x)$. A module map $F\to G$ restricts to a map $R_xF\to R_xG$ and, by the equivalence with all module maps, determines a unique map $F_x\to G_x$. Any other $F'_x$ with a specified comparison to $R_xF$ has exactly one compatible isomorphism to $F_x$, by full faithfulness. This proves natural determination and full faithfulness of the scheme comparison on each slice.

source.place: Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), forward proof applying descent.tex Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent)(1).

proof.text: Let $\alpha:y\to x$ lie over $u:T'\to T$. Relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] says that $R_yF$ is the restriction of $R_xF$ to the further slice. Under the equivalences in step 1 this is restriction from $\mathit{Sch}/T$ to $\mathit{Sch}/T'$. The base-restriction clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] therefore gives $A_{T'}(u^*F_x)\simeq R_yF\simeq A_{T'}(F_y)$. Full faithfulness gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta_\alpha:u^*F_x\simeq F_y$. It is the canonical restriction-induced map: on every open $W\subseteq T'$ its associated-sheaf map is the identity comparison between the same value of $F$ on an object above $W$. For $\beta:z\to y$ over $v:T''\to T'$, the two associated-sheaf maps obtained from $\theta_{\alpha\beta}$ and $\theta_\beta\circ v^*\theta_\alpha$ both compare restriction to $\mathcal C/z$; relocalization is sectionwise the identity and the base-restriction comparison in the cited equivalence is compatible with composition. They are equal, and faithfulness gives equality of the module maps under $(uv)^*\simeq v^*u^*$. Identity arrows and naturality for a map $F\to G$ follow in the same way from identity restriction and its commuting naturality square. Thus the coherence is for the actual canonical tensor comparisons.

On the slice over $x$, the structure sheaf is the ring sheaf of $\mathit{Sch}/T$ from step 1. The structure-module clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] thus identifies it with $\mathcal O_T$. For quasi-coherent $F,G$, [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] gives $R_x(F\otimes G)\simeq R_xF\otimes R_xG$. Substituting the counits of step 2 and then the tensor comparison of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence] identifies this sheaf with $A_T(F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}G_x)$. It is quasi-coherent on every slice, so $F\otimes G$ is quasi-coherent: a local presentation on the slice over an arbitrary object is already the local presentation required at that object. Full faithfulness gives $(F\otimes G)_x\simeq F_x\otimes G_x$. On local tensors the comparison sends the two restricted sections to their tensor section, by the formulas in the two cited nodes. This fixes the canonical tensor identification and its naturality.

source.place: descent.tex Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits)(7); sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) for localization.

proof.text: Let $f:F\to G$ be locally surjective. On each slice the same lifting covers show that $R_xf$ is locally surjective. Write $f_x:F_x\to G_x$ for its ordinary comparison and $Q_x=\operatorname{Coker}(f_x)$ in Zariski module sheaves. This is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. By the ambient-cokernel clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence], $A_T(Q_x)\simeq\operatorname{Coker}(R_xf)=0$: a locally surjective sheaf map has zero cokernel because the sheafified quotient is locally zero. The inverse of the equivalence gives $Q_x=0$. The cokernel description in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] then says every section of $G_x$ lifts Zariski locally, that is, $f_x$ is surjective. Conversely suppose all $f_x$ are surjective. Then each $Q_x=0$, so the same ambient-cokernel identity makes each $R_xf$ locally surjective. Given a section of $G(x)$, use its local lifts at the terminal object of $\mathcal C/x$ and forget the arrows to $x$. This produces an fppf lifting cover of $x$ in $\mathcal C$. This is precisely local surjectivity of $f$. Only cokernels are used; no left exactness of $A_T$ is assumed.

source.place: descent.tex Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits)(3),(4), contrasted with (6); local sheaf surjectivity via cokernels.

proof.text: Finally let $a:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be any functor over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. By [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image], $H=F\circ a$ is a module sheaf and its functor is the tensor pullback on the big ringed fppf topoi. To check its quasi-coherence directly, fix $d$ over $T$ and a presentation cover $\{x_i\to a(d)\}$ for $F$. Lift each underlying map $T_i\to T$ to $d_i\to d$. The lifting axiom [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] supplies the unique isomorphism $a(d_i)\simeq x_i$ over $a(d)$, since both lift the same base arrow. The objects $d_i$ cover $d$. On each slice the induced functor $\mathcal D/d_i\to\mathcal C/x_i$ is again a functor of categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Its module precomposition preserves small free sums, the structure module and cokernels by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. Apply it to the chosen exact presentation on $\mathcal C/x_i$; it gives an exact free presentation of $H|_{d_i}$. Thus $H$ is quasi-coherent by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. All the operations above allow arbitrary small indexing sets and arbitrary scheme arrows; no geometric flatness, algebraicity or finiteness was invoked.
